CDISC ARS export and import

Source: vignettes/articles/ars.Rmd
ars.Rmd

The specs stay the source; CDISC’s Analysis Results Standard (ARS v1.0) is written from them, and anyone’s ARS can be read back into them. The JSON is the form to exchange; CDISC’s Excel template is written for people to read.

library(tflspec)
df <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

The specs

An ARD spec, as in the article The ARD spec, plus a report spec for the outputs’ titles. ARS needs one thing the spec does not guess: each analysis’s purpose (PRIMARY / SECONDARY / EXPLORATORY OUTCOME MEASURE) is the SAP’s decision – fill the purpose column, or give tfl_ars(purpose = ) for the rows left blank. reason defaults to SPECIFIED IN SAP.

ard_spec <- tfl_ard_spec(list(
  study = df(key = c("id", "study_id"), value = c("USUBJID", "XYZ-ONC-01")),
  datasets = df(dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"),
                path = c("data/adsl.rds", "data/adae.rds")),
  populations = df(population_id = "SAF", dataset = "ADSL",
                   where = 'SAFFL == "Y"'),
  analyses = df(
    output_id = c("T-14-1-1", "T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"),
    analysis_id = c("AGE", "SEX", "TEAE"),
    method = c("continuous", "categorical", "hierarchical"),
    dataset = c(NA, NA, "ADAE"),
    population_id = "SAF",
    where = c(NA, NA, 'TRTEMFL == "Y"'),
    by = "TRT01A",
    variables = c("AGE", "SEX", "AEBODSYS | AEDECOD"),
    purpose = "PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE")))

report_spec <- tfl_table_spec(
  report = df(output_id = c("T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1")),
  titles = df(output_id = c("T-14-1-1", "T-14-3-1"), line = 1,
              center = c("Demographic Characteristics",
                         "Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events")))

Writing ARS 

ars <- tfl_ars(ard_spec, report_spec = report_spec)
tfl_check_ars(ars)      # 0 rows: valid (with jsonvalidate: CDISC's schema too)
#> [1] part    field   problem
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

What ARS has no place for – and what was added to make it complete – is listed with the reason, never dropped or added silently:

knitr::kable(tfl_ars_unmapped(ars))
where item reason
T-14-1-1 denominator added An_T-14-1-1_GROUPN_TRT01A, the subject count by group the percentages divide by
T-14-3-1 denominator added An_T-14-3-1_GROUPN_TRT01A, the subject count by group the percentages divide by 
json <- tfl_write_ars_json(ars, file.path(tempdir(), "xyz_onc_01_ars.json"))
cat(readLines(json, n = 20), sep = "\n")
#> {
#>   "id": "XYZ-ONC-01",
#>   "name": "XYZ-ONC-01",
#>   "version": 1,
#>   "mainListOfContents": {
#>     "name": "List of Planned Analyses",
#>     "contentsList": {
#>       "listItems": [
#>         {
#>           "name": "Demographic Characteristics",
#>           "level": 1,
#>           "order": 1,
#>           "outputId": "T-14-1-1",
#>           "sublist": {
#>             "listItems": [
#>               {
#>                 "name": "Number of subjects",
#>                 "level": 2,
#>                 "order": 1,
#>                 "analysisId": "An_T-14-1-1_GROUPN_TRT01A"

tfl_write_ars_xlsx(ars, path) writes CDISC’s Excel template, for people to read.

A report’s analysis data

An analysis that reads one of its report’s analysis data (data, see The ARD spec) is written with that data’s conditions: the where of each row it is made from, joined into one WhereClause on the ADaM dataset, and the population of the data it starts from. What a WhereClause cannot say – subjects, derive, code … – is listed by tfl_ars_unmapped(), as above.

adata <- df(output_id = "T-14-3-2",
            data_id = c("adae_teae", "adae_ser"),
            from = c("ADAE", "adae_teae"),
            population_id = c("SAF", NA),
            where = c('TRTEMFL == "Y"', 'AESER == "Y"'))
analyses <- df(output_id = "T-14-3-2", analysis_id = "SER",
               method = "hierarchical", data = "adae_ser", by = "TRT01A",
               variables = "AEBODSYS | AEDECOD",
               purpose = "PRIMARY OUTCOME MEASURE")
sheets <- unclass(ard_spec)[c("study", "datasets", "populations")]
ard_spec2 <- tfl_ard_spec(c(sheets,
                            list(analysis_data = adata, analyses = analyses)))
ars2 <- tfl_ars(ard_spec2)
tfl_check_ars(ars2)
#> [1] part    field   problem
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

An output that prints another’s analyses

A figure that prints a table’s median and hazard ratio has no analyses of its own. tfl_ars(references = ) names such outputs – output_id, source (the output whose analyses it prints) and analysis_id – and writes each as an ARS Output whose list-of-contents item points at the source’s analyses, which are not written twice. One whose source the ARS does not have is listed by tfl_ars_unmapped().

Running it with siera

profile = "siera" writes ARS that siera can run – still valid CDISC ARS, with an R code template per method. tfl_ars_ard() runs it (siera writes and runs one programme per output) and gives its ARD, a round trip to compare with the ARD tflspec builds:

ars_s <- tfl_ars(ard_spec, profile = "siera")
ard <- tfl_ars_ard(ars_s, adam)   # adam: a named list of datasets, or a folder

An analysis siera has no template for (a test other than chi-square, missing, mean_ci, custom …) is left out and listed by tfl_ars_unmapped().

Reading anyone’s ARS

tfl_read_ars_json() reads an ARS JSON – one written elsewhere, by another tool – and tfl_ars_to_specs() turns it into specs: $ard, $report (and with table = TRUE, $table: the groupings’ levels). ARS has no ADaM paths, so datasets$path is filled in before the ARD spec runs; what has no place in the specs is in attr(, "unmapped").

sp <- tfl_ars_to_specs(tfl_read_ars_json(json))
sp$ard$analyses[, c("output_id", "analysis_id", "method", "by", "variables")]
#>   output_id analysis_id       method     by          variables
#> 1  T-14-1-1         AGE   continuous TRT01A                AGE
#> 2  T-14-1-1         SEX  categorical TRT01A                SEX
#> 3  T-14-3-1        TEAE hierarchical TRT01A AEBODSYS | AEDECOD
sp$report$titles[, c("output_id", "line", "center")]
#>   output_id line                            center
#> 1  T-14-1-1    1       Demographic Characteristics
#> 2  T-14-3-1    1 Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events

There is no way back from an ARD alone (it has no data paths, populations or conditions); an existing study’s analyses come in through ARS.
